title: Whole-number floats and exact usage reconciliation
why: Python's `json.dumps` writes an integral float as `100.0`; JavaScript's `JSON.stringify` writes `100`. The JS viewer therefore has to wrap every percentage in `PyFloat` (see `js/src/viewer/pyjson.ts`) to reproduce Python's spelling in the embedded payload, and the CLI has to format `100.0%` the same way on both sides. Turn 1 has a single block, so its share is exactly 100.0%; turn 2 has two labels; turn 3's provider usage is set to the block total so reconciliation prints an exact zero delta. Any regression in the float-spelling shim shows up here as a one-character diff.
